name: BaikalDB
tagline: Baidu's MySQL-compatible distributed HTAP database on RocksDB and Raft, with full-text and vector indexes.
description: BaikalDB is a distributed SQL database from Baidu, open-sourced in 2018, that speaks the MySQL protocol and dialect so applications can move from MySQL with few changes. It separates a stateless SQL layer from Raft-replicated storage regions on RocksDB, built with Baidu's brpc and braft libraries, and borrows design ideas from TiDB and Impala. Beyond OLTP it adds inverted full-text indexes, a columnar engine, MPP execution, querying of Parquet files and, in 2026 releases, vector indexes (IVF and PQ variants), cosine-similarity functions, array columns, column-level TTL and an optional storage-compute separated mode. It is actively developed (v5.0.0, June 2026), though most documentation and community discussion are in Chinese.

scale.notes: Data is split into Raft-replicated regions that split and move automatically; positioned for petabyte-scale structured data.

strengths: MySQL protocol compatibility eases migration from sharded MySQL
Raft-replicated regions give automatic sharding, failover and rebalancing
Full-text inverted indexes and vector indexes in the same SQL engine
Columnar engine and MPP execution for analytical queries alongside OLTP
Permissive Apache 2.0 license with frequent 2026 releases
weaknesses: Documentation, release notes and community are mostly in Chinese
Small ecosystem outside Baidu compared with TiDB or CockroachDB
Some features (e.g. storage-compute separation) only target Baidu's internal file system
useCases: HTAP reporting on live transactional data
Combining SQL filters with full-text or vector similarity search
notIdealFor: Small single-node deployments where MySQL or PostgreSQL suffice
